fields.companyDescription: Hotel Equities (CALA) is the Caribbean & Latin America division of Hotel Equities, focused on third-party hotel and resort management in the region. It combines local leadership and regional operating support with Hotel Equities' broader management platform. The division is positioned around all-inclusive resorts and urban/lifestyle hotels.
fields.headquarters: Parent HQ: Atlanta, Georgia, United States; CALA in-market leadership in Miami, Mexico, Dominican Republic, and Washington DC area
fields.missionStatement: Fill the long-standing gap in third-party hospitality management for owners in the Caribbean and Latin America with local leadership, purpose-built infrastructure, and a performance-driven, owner-aligned approach.
fields.companyHistory: Hotel Equities was founded in 1989 and has grown into a hotel management and development company operating across the U.S., Canada, the Caribbean, and Latin America. In 2024, Hotel Equities formed a strategic partnership with Trust Hospitality to launch and scale its dedicated CALA division, with a focus on all-inclusive resorts and urban/lifestyle hotels. Industry press reported Juan Corvinos as president of the division in 2025.
fields.differentiators: Local leadership in region; purpose-built CALA infrastructure; owner-aligned operating model; focus on all-inclusive and urban/lifestyle hotels; third-party management specialization; regional footprint across Caribbean and Latin America
fields.managementPhilosophy: Owner-aligned, performance-driven operating approach with regional leadership and local market knowledge
fields.propertyTypes: Full Service; Select Service; Resort; Boutique; Lifestyle; All-inclusive
fields.specificMarkets: HE CALA has open and pipeline hotels in the Dominican Republic, Turks & Caicos, Curaçao, Mexico, Trinidad & Tobago, Dominica, and Costa Rica, with additional references to Riviera Maya and Mexico City.
fields.mkt_narrative_depth: HE CALA is building a regional third-party management platform for Caribbean and Latin American owners. Public materials show a mix of open hotels and signed projects, with emphasis on leisure destinations and resort markets. The geography includes both island resort markets and larger gateway or beach destinations. The footprint appears to be expanding from a small base, rather than representing a long-established regional network.
fields.mkt_signal_gateway: Resort markets with some gateway-city exposure
fields.mkt_signal_mix: Resort-heavy with urban/lifestyle adjacency and all-inclusive focus
fields.overview_signal_1_value: 17 CALA hotels (5 open, 12 pipeline) across Dominican Republic, Turks & Caicos, Curaçao, Mexico, Trinidad & Tobago, Dominica, and Costa Rica (per HE public posts, Jan 2026).
fields.overview_signal_2_value: Parent platform: 64 franchise partner brands; CALA portfolio includes Marriott, Hilton, Hyatt, and soft-brand/collection formats.
fields.overview_signal_3_value: In-market leadership hubs: Miami, Mexico, Dominican Republic; regional roles across operations, finance, sales & marketing, HR, IT/openings, and shared services.
fields.cap_profile_operational: HE CALA is organized around local leadership and regional execution in Caribbean and Latin America markets. Public materials indicate a focus on hotel opening, transition, and ongoing management support for leisure and lifestyle assets. The division appears intended to give owners regional coverage while leveraging the parent company's broader operating platform.
fields.cap_profile_commercial: The commercial model appears to combine regional sales coverage with parent-platform support for revenue management, distribution, and brand relationships. Public statements emphasize performance-driven management, which usually implies tighter coordination between operations and commercial disciplines. Specific system architecture was not publicly identified.
fields.cap_profile_transition: CALA public materials show active pre-opening and pipeline work, including projects in multiple island and resort markets. This suggests the division is being used for both opening new assets and moving branded properties into operation. The first Costa Rica opening was publicly announced in March 2026.
fields.cap_card_asset_positioning: CALA is best framed as a regional operating platform for leisure-oriented hotel owners seeking third-party management in Caribbean and Latin America markets. The division is concentrated in resort and lifestyle assets rather than broad urban scale. It is therefore positioned more as a specialized regional operator than a full global platform.
fields.cap_card_service_diff: The visible differentiator is regional leadership tied to a broader parent company platform. Public materials emphasize local knowledge, owner alignment, and a dedicated CALA structure rather than a generic remote management model.
fields.cap_card_execution_rel: The division's language is explicitly owner-facing, with emphasis on value creation and local execution. For institutional owners, that usually indicates a relationship model centered on reporting, accountability, and market responsiveness. The public record does not yet show a long operating history in CALA, so depth should be viewed as emerging rather than legacy.
fields.cap_card_governance: Public sources do not publish cadence details, committee structure, or reporting pack formats. The safest conclusion is that governance is likely structured but not externally documented.
fields.cap_deep_execution_infra: The division describes purpose-built infrastructure and local leadership, but no detailed technology or organizational chart was published. Public evidence is strongest on market presence and leadership rather than back-office systems.
fields.brand_narrative_compliance: Brand compliance appears to be handled through standard branded-hotel operating practices, supported by a third-party management platform and regional leadership. Public materials do not describe a proprietary compliance system.
fields.brand_narrative_relationship: HE CALA appears to work within major franchise and soft-brand ecosystems, including Marriott, Hilton, and Hyatt family brands. The public footprint indicates brand-specific operating experience rather than a single exclusive brand relationship.
fields.ov_card_discipline: HE CALA presents as a comparatively disciplined, owner-aligned regional platform, but the public record is still short because the division launched in 2025. The strongest evidence is the division's explicit structure, local leadership, and the move from launch to open hotels plus pipeline within months.
fields.ov_card_commercial: The company says it combines global best practices with regional knowledge, and the broader Hotel Equities platform references training, brand relationships, and commercial support. Exact commercial staffing and system depth were not verified.
fields.ov_card_communication: Public materials suggest an owner-facing communication style, but no reporting calendar or dashboard structure was published. The safest characterization is structured but not fully public.
fields.ov_card_flexibility: The division appears designed to be flexible across resort, lifestyle, and all-inclusive settings in multiple countries. That suggests adaptability, though contract customization and fee flexibility were not disclosed.
fields.ov_card_risk: The principal risk factor for an owner evaluating CALA is limited public operating history as a stand-alone regional division. The main continuity strength is the backing of the larger Hotel Equities organization.
fields.ownerEngagementNarrative: HE CALA is framed as an owner-aligned third-party management platform with regional leadership and local knowledge. For owners, the practical implication is a leaner regional operating model backed by a larger parent company, but the public record does not yet show a long CALA track record.
fields.specializations: All-inclusive resorts; urban/lifestyle hotels; Caribbean and Latin America regional operations; resort-heavy leisure markets; pre-opening and transition support
fields.lead_narrative_regional: Public materials emphasize deep investment in local leadership and purpose-built regional infrastructure. The leadership model appears centered on a president for CALA plus supporting operations and development roles.
fields.regionalTeams: Local leadership pods supported by a regional CALA team and parent-company platform
fields.brandsPortfolioDetail: Confirmed CALA-related public examples include LXR Hotels & Resorts: 1 hotel (Amaris Grace Bay, Turks & Caicos); Autograph Collection: 1 hotel (Donoma Las Terrenas Beach Resort & Spa, Dominican Republic). Public CALA posts also reference additional forthcoming projects in Curacao, Mexico City, Riviera Maya, Trinidad & Tobago, Dominica, and Costa Rica.
